newsitem.title: USA: ALPINE SKIING-WINDS FORCE POSTPONEMENT OF WOMEN'S SUPER-G.
newsitem.headline: ALPINE SKIING-WINDS FORCE POSTPONEMENT OF WOMEN'S SUPER-G.

text.p: Wind gusts of more than 50 kph (30 mph) forced postponement of the women's World Cup super-g race at Mammoth Mountain Ski Area Thursday.

The race, originally slated to begin at 10 a.m. (1800 gmt), was delayed until noon, then further delayed until 2:30 p.m. Race officials and members of the race jury eventually voted unanimously to postpone the event until 9 a.m. (1700 gmt) Friday.

"Strong tail winds on the part of the course known as Terry's Road were a safety concernJeff Nelson of the Mammoth Mountain Race Department. Officials also said sporadic wind gusts might cause a unfair race.
A slalom race, already on the schedule for Friday, was to follow shortly after the super-g.
The two-event stop of the women's World Cup in Mammoth marks the tour's return to the United States and is the last World Cup event before the World Cup finals March 12-16 at Vail, Colorado.

Overall standings leader Pernilla Wiberg of Sweden headed the 120-plus pack of skiers with 1,555 points heading into Friday's two events. Katja Seizinger of Germany was close behind with 1,004 points.

Mammoth Mountain hosted a World Cup event once before. In 1994, the women's tour raced here in super-g and slalom. Mammoth is the only ski resort in California to host World Cup skiing in the last ten years.
